source.name: Desuarchive /mlp/ yearly export 1-42799493 (2025)
source.short-desc: Desuarchive /mlp/ post export as newline-delimited JSON, uploaded 2025-11-14
source.capture:
One 6.8GB payload, base_1_42799493.ndjson.gz, plus IA bookkeeping. No image payloads, so no download.exclude is needed. Surveyed against archive.org/metadata (5 files).

FORMAT IS NDJSON, and it is very nearly the standard staged format already -- which is why it gets a converter rather than the reader getting a second shape. Three differences, none visible from the field names: the numbers are STRINGS ("num":"1", "op":"1") while timestamp is not; `board` is an OBJECT, {"name":"Pony","shortname":"mlp"}, not the slug; and media_filename/media_hash are NESTED inside a `media` object. _payloads/asagi-export-to-ndjson normalises all three during prepare.

The title 'yearly_1_42799493 (2025)' and the identifier suggest a post-number range export (posts 1 through 42,799,493) rather than a calendar year, so the name is misleading — treat the range as covering /mlp/ from the start of Desuarchive's coverage up to that post number, and verify against the actual records rather than the title.

SCOPE: /mlp/ only. That board is currently absent from the corpus, so this adds a board rather than deepening one, but it does nothing for the /g/ post-2017 gap or the /r9k/ single-year problem that are currently driving source selection.

BEFORE WRITING AN ADAPTER, check whether Desuarchive publishes the same export for other boards. A per-board NDJSON series would make the new adapter worth far more than one board — and desuarchive_db_201909, already in the registry, is the same archive in mysqldump form and may cover /mlp/ too, in which case this item may be redundant. Diff the two before ingesting both.

--- SURVEYED AFTER STAGING (records read, not inferred) ---

6.8GB gz expands to 68.5GB of NDJSON. Records are ASAGI-SHAPED, one JSON object per line, and carry every field the SQL adapters read plus more: doc_id, num, subnum, thread_num, op, timestamp, timestamp_expired, capcode, email, name, trip, title, comment, poster_hash, poster_country, sticky, locked, deleted, nreplies, nimages, fourchan_date, comment_sanitized, comment_processed, formatted, title_processed, name_processed, email_processed, trip_processed, poster_hash_processed, poster_country_name, poster_country_name_processed, extra_data, exif, media, board.

A `board` FIELD IS PRESENT, so unlike the posts+threads dumps this needs no join — every record is self-describing. Use `comment`; comment_sanitized and comment_processed are pre-rendered variants.

THE TIMESTAMP CONVENTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN 2019 SQL DUMPS, AND GETTING IT WRONG COSTS 4-5 HOURS ON EVERY POST. Here `timestamp` is TRUE UTC and must NOT go through nyWallToUtc. Verified at both ends of the file against the record's own fourchan_date display string, which is New-York wall time:
  num 1        ts 1329457190 = 2012-02-17 05:39 UTC = 00:39 NY, fourchan_date '2/17/12(Fri)0:39'
  num 42799492 ts 1763146454 = 2025-11-14 18:54 UTC = 13:54 NY, fourchan_date '11/14/25(Fri)13:54'
By contrast desuarchive_db_201909, the same archive in mysqldump form, stores New-York wall time — measured against 2,500 posts shared with installgentoo. Desuarchive evidently migrated its storage to UTC between 2019 and 2025. Never assume one export's convention from another's, even within one archive.

THE IDENTIFIER IS A POST-NUMBER RANGE, NOT A YEAR, which the title 'yearly_1_42799493 (2025)' obscures: records run from num 1 (moot's /mlp/ founding post, 2012-02-17) to num 42,799,492 (2025-11-14). So this is the board's FULL history up to the export date, not one year of it — which makes it a superset of whatever /mlp/ desuarchive_db_201909 holds, and that item's mlp.sql.bz2 is probably redundant once this is ingested. Diff before ingesting both.

An adapter is still needed (nothing here reads NDJSON), but it is the simplest one in the registry: JSON.parse per line, direct field mapping, no join, no timezone conversion.
